liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **The Other One** (4 reviews): Runs just under an hour, with the band playing as one unit and covering lots of ground; Described as the longest version on record, over 40 minutes, showcasing Garcia's artistry [3][4][13][14]
- **Bird Song** (1 review): Called fabulous, one of many strong versions that month [13]
- **Tennessee Jed** (1 review): Reviewer considers it the best version the band played [7]
- **Playing in the Band** (1 review): Nearly spacey, yet still grounded; Half Step is laid back and nice [7]
- **Truckin'** (1 review): Garcia charges out of the vocals into one of the typical 1972 mini-jams; this one runs hot [3]
- **Mississippi Half Step** (1 review): A nice version, noted as one of the first ten ever played [6]
- **He's Gone** (1 review): The He's Gone into The Other One into Sing Me Back Home sequence is called incredible [3]
- **Sugar Magnolia** (1 review): Reviewer's favorite version, with Garcia ripping it up around minutes five to six [7]

## The recordings

- **gd72-09-17.sbd.hamilton.154.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 23 songs; 203 min; rated 4.29/5 by 7 [1]. Said about its sound: Known flaws: Saturday Night missing and a small digital glitch during Uncle John's Band [1]
- **gd1972-09-17.aud-wolfson.minches.28165.shnf**: audience recording; 24 songs; 194 min; rated 4.62/5 by 16 [2]. Said about its sound: Decent audience recording with vocals somewhat hit or miss; Audience tape runs slightly fast, not enough to matter, and is unusually good for a 1972 audience recording; Audience recording quality is not the greatest [6][8][9][13]

## Around the show

- Reviewer moved in with his girlfriend that day, brought Baltimore friends, and stood on a chair holding a microphone up [5]
- Felt like the highlights of every 1972 show packed into a single night [5]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd72-09-17.sbd.hamilton.154.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Reviewer got an SHN copy well before the official release; Soundboard master to cassette, DAT, CD, then SHN; extracted and encoded by G.S. Hamilton from a Hollister seed [1][4]
- **gd1972-09-17.aud-wolfson.minches.28165.shnf**: taped by Cary Wolfson; transferred by David Minches; source: Audience (taper Cary Wolfson) > Cass > DAT > SHN [2]. Also: Taper used a Sony TC-124 with a one-point stereo microphone [12]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Jerry Garcia: [Grateful Dead Poster 1972-09-17 - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/image/grateful-dead-poster-1972-09-17-17/) [16]
- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Baltimore Civic Center - September 17, 1972](https://www.dead.net/show/september-17-1972) [17]
